title: Why airplane mode exists, and what it actually does
description: Airplane mode switches off your phone's transmitters. The rule behind it is older than smartphones.

scenes.sub: the rule is older than smartphones
scenes.say: Every flight, you switch on airplane mode. But why does it exist at all?

steps: You can switch Wi-Fi back on
scenes.say: Airplane mode turns off your phone's transmitters. Cellular, and by default Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Many phones let you turn Wi-Fi or Bluetooth back on afterward, for in-flight Wi-Fi or headphones.

Two rules sit behind it. In 1991, the FCC banned most in-flight cell use, citing interference with ground networks. The FAA separately says signals could interfere with aircraft communication and navigation.
Studies commissioned by the FAA in 2006 and 2012 found no evidence that cell signals interfere with aircraft systems. Even so, regulators kept the rules, citing caution.

scenes.sub: rules vary by airline and country
scenes.say: Rules do vary now, so follow the crew's instructions. Caution, built on old rules. Follow for more everyday tech explained.
